findings.action: Require evidence that a roadmap actually closed before adoption before classifying it as historical. closeoutScopeHistorical accepts the current legacy enabled/cutoff shortcut or any recorded bundle approval, without checking whether that bundle sealed CloseoutReview. A roadmap approved under schema 5 and subsequently marked done without a receipt therefore becomes historical: closeoutReviewGate returns nil, getCloseoutState does not require a receipt, and CLI close can report already-satisfied. The enabled=false branch can also suppress adopted always and recorded negative reviews on a done roadmap. This violates R2/R4/R5 and the prospective-history contract. Apply the sealed pre-adoption-plan distinction used by milestoneClosedBeforeAdoption and cover both post-adoption approval and disabled-policy cases.

Emit a valid optional association default. The new template writes adrs: followed only by an inline explanatory comment; the distributed scaffold has the same line. cmdNewRoadmap preserves it, but associationList reads the raw comment as the value and rejects it as outside a list. Filling the required roadmap fields while leaving this optional field untouched consequently makes when-justified evaluation unknown and prevents close. Omit the optional declaration or emit a parseable empty list with its explanation on a separate comment line, and exercise the generated template through the evaluator.

Preserve the complete Markdown fence delimiter and validate its closing syntax. markdownWithoutCode truncates every opener to three characters. For valid Markdown consisting of an opening four-backtick fence, a literal three-backtick line inside it, example text, the closing four-backtick fence, and then a real ADR link, the three-backtick line prematurely closes this filter's fence and the real closing delimiter opens another one. The actual association is discarded without a diagnostic. A two-member roadmap whose sole ADR association is that link consequently receives Known=true and Required=false under when-justified, violating R3. Cover longer fences and real links following them.

Normalize association keys consistently with SplitFrontmatter before tracking their presence and duplicates. SplitFrontmatter splits at the colon and trims the key, whereas associationList recognizes only a literal unindented key followed immediately by a colon. Thus adrs : [adr:decision.md], or the equivalent roadmaps declaration, is silently absent here despite being recognized by the repository's frontmatter reader. With two canonical members and no other association, when-justified grants an exemption without a diagnostic. Differently spaced duplicate keys also escape duplicate detection. This is the remaining R11-N39 gap: recognize normalized keys and reject ambiguity before proving association absence.
